answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity: before an agent may vote or earn, it locks real collateral in a public vault, and only identities with a locked bond count. A fake account that tries to wander between fresh names must post new capital for every alias, so the harbor of trusted peers stays small. Reputation forms an atlas of costly, repeated endorsements, so an attacker must fund each forged node while rewards stay fixed - the bill rises linearly with every Sybil.
